answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar kisi muahiday (agreement) ka maqsad ya consideration ghair qanooni (unlawful) ho, to woh muahida void hota hai.
answer.explanation: Contract Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, har woh muahida jiska maqsad ya consideration ghair qanooni ho, void qarar diya jata hai. Mazeed bar-aan, agar consideration ka koi hissa bhi ghair qanooni ho, to poora muahida void ho jata hai.

citations.quote: Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or anyone or any part of anyone of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Yes, you may demand the return of a gratuitously lent item at any time, but you must indemnify the borrower if the premature return causes them a loss that exceeds the benefit they derived from the loan.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, a lender can reclaim a gratuitously lent item even if a specific time or purpose was agreed upon. However, if the borrower has acted in reliance on that loan such that an early return causes them a loss greater than the benefit they received, the lender is legally required to compensate the borrower for that excess loss.

citations.quote: The lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose. But, if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
جی ہاں، اگر معاہدے میں خلاف ورزی پر جرمانے کی رقم طے بھی ہو، تب بھی عدالت اس معاہدے کو مخصوص نفاذ (Specific Performance) کے لیے نافذ کر سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: قانون کے مطابق، اگر کوئی معاہدہ مخصوص نفاذ کے لیے مناسب ہو تو اسے نافذ کیا جا سکتا ہے، چاہے اس میں خلاف ورزی کی صورت میں ادا کی جانے والی رقم ہی کیوں نہ درج ہو۔

citations.quote: وہ معاہدہ جو بظاہر دیگر مخصوص نفاذ کے لیے مناسب ہوا سے نافذ کیا جا سکتا ہے، اگر چہ اس میں رقم درج ہو جو خلاف ورزی پر ادا کی جانی ہے، اور نادہندہ فریق اسے ادا کرنے پر راضی ہو۔

answer.short_answer: No, you cannot hold the person liable for non-performance if your failure to perform your reciprocal promise prevents them from completing the work.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a contract consists of reciprocal promises and one party fails to perform their part first, they cannot claim the performance of the other party and must compensate the other party for any loss sustained due to the non-performance.

citations.quote: When a contract consists of reciprocal promises, such that one of them cannot be performed, or that its performance cannot be claimed till the other has been performed, and the promisor of the promise last mentioned fails to perform it, such promisor cannot claim the performance of the reciprocal promise, and must make compensation to the other party to the contract for any loss which such other party may sustain by the non-performance of the contract.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Agar contract mein performance ki jagah mention nahi ki gayi aur promisee ne koi request bhi nahi ki, toh promisor ka farz hai ke woh promisee se raabta kare aur usse performance ke liye koi munasib jagah muqarrar karne ki darkhwast kare.
answer.explanation: Contract Act ki Section 49 ke mutabiq, agar kisi promise ko perform karne ke liye koi jagah tay nahi ki gayi aur promisee ki taraf se koi application (request) nahi di gayi, toh promisor ki zimmedari hai ke woh khud promisee se munasib jagah muqarrar karne ka kahe aur phir wahan performance mukammal kare.

citations.quote: When a promise is to be performed without application by the promisee, and no place is fixed for the performance of it, it is the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform it at such place.

answer.short_answer: Contract Act, 1872 ki Section 126 ke mutabiq, guarantee oral (zabani) ya written (tehreeri) dono ho sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Section 126 wazeh taur par bayan karti hai ke guarantee ka muahida oral ya written dono sooraton mein kiya ja sakta hai.

citations.quote: A guarantee may be either oral or written.

answer.short_answer: Co-sureties are liable to pay an equal share of the debt or the remaining unpaid portion, unless they have agreed otherwise by contract.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, co-sureties for the same debt are responsible for contributing equally to the liability, provided there is no specific contract between them stating a different arrangement.

citations.quote: the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, are liable, as between themselves, to pay each an equal share of the whole debt, or of that part of it which remains unpaid by the principal debtor.

answer.short_answer: عوامی راستے پر لاپرواہی سے گاڑی چلانے کی صورت میں دو سال تک قید، تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں سزائیں ہو سکتی ہیں۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 279 کے تحت، عوامی راستے پر کسی بھی گاڑی کو اس قدر لاپرواہی یا غفلت سے چلانا کہ جس سے انسانی زندگی کو خطرہ ہو یا کسی دوسرے شخص کو چوٹ لگنے کا امکان ہو، ایک قابل سزا جرم ہے۔

citations.quote: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2[two years] or with fine which may extend to 1[three] thousand rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 کے تحت کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں حملہ کرنے یا جبر مجرمانہ استعمال کرنے کی سزا ایک سال تک قید، تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں ہو سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: قانون کے مطابق جو کوئی شخص کسی دوسرے شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں اس پر حملہ کرے یا جبر مجرمانہ استعمال کرے تو اسے مذکورہ بالا سزا دی جائے گی۔

citations.quote: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to 3[three thousand rupees], or with both.

جوکوئی شخص کسیشخص پر نذکور وخص کجبس بجامیل رسکنےئ وشش میںحملہ یاجبرجرماند کرسےتوّاےکی ایکفتم کیاسزاۓ قیداتی مدت ک لیےدی جاستۓ گ جوایک سال تک بوسکتی ے یآ ا تین نزارروپ [ تک جربانےکی سزایادونوں سزا نیں دی جائنیں گی

answer.short_answer: A person who advocates for the abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty faces a punishment of rigorous imprisonment for up to ten years and a fine.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, it is an offence to advocate for the curtailment or abolition of the sovereignty of Pakistan, punishable by rigorous imprisonment of up to ten years and a fine. Additionally, courts have the authority to issue orders regarding the accused's movements, associations, and communication during the investigation or trial.

citations.quote: advocate the curtailment or abolition of the sovereignty of Pakistan in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, whether by amalgamation with the territories of neighboring States or otherwise, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.

it shall be lawful for any Court before which he may be produced in the course of the investigation or trial, to make such order as it may think fit in respect of his movements, of his association or communication with other persons, and of his activities in regard to dissemination of news, propagation of opinions, until such time as the case is finally decided.

answer.short_answer: Yes, an individual can be charged with cheating by personation even if the person they are pretending to be is imaginary.
answer.explanation: According to the Pakistan Penal Code, the offence of cheating by personation is committed regardless of whether the person being impersonated is a real or an imaginary person.

citations.quote: The offence is committed whether the in dividual personated is a real or imaginary person.

answer.short_answer: The arsh for the destruction of an organ found singly in the human body is equivalent to the value of diyat.
answer.explanation: According to Section 337Q of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, the arsh for causing itlaf (destruction) of a single organ is equal to the full value of diyat.

citations.quote: The arsh for causing itlaf of an organ which is found singly in a human body shall be equivalent to the value of diyat.

answer.short_answer: An intoxicated person who causes annoyance in a public place may be punished with simple imprisonment for up to twenty-four hours, a fine of up to thirty rupees, or both.
answer.explanation: Under Section 510 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, any person who is in a state of intoxication in a public place or a place where they are trespassing and conducts themselves in a manner that causes annoyance to others is subject to these penalties.

citations.quote: Whoever, in a state of intoxication appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to 1[thirty] rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: The maximum term of imprisonment for causing mudihah to another person is five years.
answer.explanation: Under Section 337F of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, a person who causes mudihah is liable to daman and may be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to five years as ta'zir.

citations.quote: (iv) mudihah to any person, shall be liable to daman and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years as ta'zir

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
No sufficient source found
Yes, it is a criminal offense under the Pakistan Penal Code to accept gratification for using personal influence to persuade a public servant to perform an official act.
answer.explanation: Section 163 of the Pakistan Penal Code explicitly criminalizes the act of accepting, obtaining, or attempting to obtain any gratification as a motive or reward for inducing a public servant to perform or forbear from an official act through the exercise of personal influence.

citations.quote: Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for in ducing, by the exercise of personal influence, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act... shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar National Assembly dissolve ho jaye to Federal Government kharchon ke liye funds authorize kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Dastoor ke mutabiq, jab National Assembly dissolve ho, to Federal Government Federal Consolidated Fund se kisi bhi mali saal mein char mah se zyada ki muddat ke liye kharchon ko authorize kar sakti hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: at any time when the National Assembly stands dissolved, the Federal Government may authorize expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund in respect of the estimated expenditure for a period not exceeding four months in any financial year

answer.short_answer: If a member of a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, their seat in the Assembly becomes vacant on the day they enter upon their office.
answer.explanation: According to Article 103 of the Constitution, a Governor cannot be a member of a Provincial Assembly, and the appointment of such a member to the office of Governor triggers the vacation of their legislative seat upon assuming the new role.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: if a member of 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, his seat in 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or, as the case may be, the Provincial Assembly shall become vacant on the day he enters upon his office.

answer.short_answer: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 ke Article 203F ke tehat, Federation ya Province ke liye appeal karne ki muddat faislay ke baad chhay (6) mahine hai.
answer.explanation: Article 203F(1) ke mutabiq, aam taur par appeal 60 din mein ki ja sakti hai, lekin Federation ya Province ke liye yeh muddat barha kar chhay mahine kar di gayi hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Provided that an appeal on behalf of the Federation or of a Province may be preferred within six months of such decision.

answer.short_answer: جی نہیں، پارلیمنٹ کی کارروائی کو کسی طریقہ کار کی بے قاعدگی کی بنیاد پر عدالت میں چیلنج نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔
answer.explanation: دستورِ پاکستان کے مطابق، پارلیمنٹ کی کسی بھی کارروائی کے جواز پر ضابطہ کار کی کسی بے قاعدگی کی بنیاد پر اعتراض نہیں کیا جا سکتا، اور عدالتیں پارلیمنٹ کی کارروائی کی تحقیقات نہیں کریں گی۔

citations.quote: مجلسِ شوریٰ (پارلیمنٹ) میں کسی بھی کارروائی کے جواز پر ضابطہ کار کی کسی بے قاعدگی کی بناء پر اعتراض نہیں کیا جائے گا۔
عدالتیں مجلسِ شوریٰ (پارلیمنٹ) کی کارروائی کی تحقیقات نہیں کریں گی۔

answer.short_answer: No, a court cannot validate an act of high treason against the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Constitution explicitly prohibits any court, including the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and any High Court, from validating an act of high treason.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: An act of high treason mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) shall not be validated by any court including the Federal Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and a High Court.

Ji haan, Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ki Section 39(2) ke tehat, decree pass karne wali court apni marzi se (of its own motion) kisi subordinate court ko execution ke liye decree bhej sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Section 39(2) wazeh taur par ijazat deta hai ke court khud se kisi subordinate court ko decree transfer kar sakti hai.

citations.quote: The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction.

answer.short_answer: No, a public officer cannot be arrested or have their property attached in a lawsuit regarding their official duties, except in execution of a decree.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a public officer sued for acts done in their official capacity is exempt from arrest and the attachment of their property, unless such actions are taken to execute a court decree.

citations.quote: In a suit instituted against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done by him in his official capacity__ (a) the defendant shall not be liable to arrest nor his property to attachment otherwise than in execution of a decree
Provided that the defendant shall not be liable to arrest, nor his property to attachment otherwise than in execution of a decree.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
جی ہاں، کوڈ آف سول پروسیجر 1908 کی سیکشن 86A کے تحت مخصوص حالات میں سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی کی جا سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف کارروائی صرف ان صورتوں میں ممکن ہے جو نجی جائیداد، وراثت، یا پاکستان میں ان کے سرکاری فرائض سے ہٹ کر کسی پیشہ ورانہ یا تجارتی سرگرمی سے متعلق ہوں۔

citations.quote: No proceeding in any Court shall lie against a diplomatic agent except in a case relating to__ (a) any private immoveable property situated in Pakistan held by him in his private capacity and not on behalf of the sending State for the purpose of the mission ; (b) a succession in which the diplomatic agent is involved as executor, administrator, heir or legatee as a private person and not on behalf of the sending State; (c) any professional or commercial activity exercised by the diplomatic agent in Pakistan outside his official functions.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a High Court may order the execution of a decree before the costs of the suit have been ascertained by taxation.
answer.explanation: If a High Court deems it necessary, it can order the immediate execution of a decree passed in its original civil jurisdiction, excluding the portion related to costs, which can be executed once the costs are ascertained.

citations.quote: Where any 3* High Court considers it necessary that a decree passed in the exercise of its original civil jurisdiction should be executed before the amount of the costs incurred in the suit can be ascertained by taxation, the Court may order that the decree shall be executed forthwith, except as to so much thereof as relates to the costs

answer.short_answer: Yes, the court has the discretion to allow you to pay the deficient court fees at any stage of the proceedings.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, if a document is filed without the required court fees, the court may permit the payment of the deficiency at any time. Once paid, the document is treated as if the fees had been paid initially.

citations.quote: the Court may, in its discretion, at any stage, allow the person, by whom such fee is payable, to pay the whole or part, as the case may be, of such court-fee; and upon such payment the document, in respect of which such fee is payable, shall have the same force and effect as if such fee had been paid in the first instance.

answer.short_answer: Income derived from a business or source that has ceased is treated as if the business or source had not ceased at the time the income was derived, provided it would have been chargeable to tax under the Ordinance had it been derived before the cessation.
answer.explanation: Under Section 72 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, if income is received from a source that has ceased either before or during the tax year, the Ordinance applies to that income as if the source were still active, assuming the income would have been taxable had the source not ceased.

citations.quote: this Ordinance shall apply to the income on the basis that the business, activity, investment or other source had not ceased at the time the income was derived.

answer.short_answer: No, two individuals cannot be considered associates solely because they are both employees of the same company.
answer.explanation: The Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 explicitly states that two persons shall not be treated as associates merely because they are both employees of the same third person.

citations.quote: Two persons shall not be associates solely by reason of the fact that one person is an employee of the other or both persons are employees of a third person.

answer.short_answer: No, mutual funds and insurance companies are not subject to the same capital gain tax computation rules under Section 100B as other entities.
answer.explanation: While Section 100B generally mandates that capital gains on listed securities be computed under the Eighth Schedule, it explicitly excludes mutual funds, banking companies, and insurance companies from these provisions. Instead, these entities are required to compute and determine capital gains according to the mechanism prescribed under Section 37A, though they must still deposit tax on the capital gain as per the Ordinance's applicable provisions.

citations.quote: The provisions of sub–section (1) shall not apply to the following persons or class of persons, namely:- (a) a mutual fund; banking company and an insurance company subject to tax under the Fourth Schedule

NCCPL, in case of banking company, insurance company and mutual funds, shall compute and determine the capital gain as per the mechanism prescribed under section 37A; however, these entities shall continue to deposit tax on the amount of capital gain as per the applicable provisions of this Ordinance.

Ji haan, agar aapko kisi shakhs par terrorism ya us se mutaliq juraaim ka shaq ho, to aap police ko itla dene ke liye qanooni taur par tawun karne ke paband hain.
answer.explanation: Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 ke tehat, agar koi shakhs police ko itla deta hai ke koi raqam ya jaidad dehshat gardi se hasil ki gayi hai, to woh police ke sath tawun karne ka mujaz hai. Is ke ilawa, agar koi shakhs dehshat gardi ki tafteesh ke dauran kisi maloomat ka inkeshaf karta hai jo us ke shaq ya yaqeen par mabni ho, to woh is qanoon ke tehat police ke sath tawun kar sakta hai.

citations.quote: پولیس کے ساتھ تعاون - دفعات ۱۱ح تا ۱۱ک کے تحت سرگرمیوں میں شریک کوئی شخص مجرم قرار نہیں دیا جائے گا اگر وہ کسی ایسے پولیس افسر کو واضح رضامندی کے ساتھ معلومات فراہم کرے کہ --- (الف) اس کے شک یا یقین کے مطابق رقم یا جائیداد دہشت گردی سے حاصل ہونے والی رقم یا جائیداد ہے اور (ب) جو معلومات وہ فراہم کرتا ہے وہ اس کے شک یا یقین کی اساس ہیں

answer.short_answer: A person sentenced by an Anti-terrorism Court must file an appeal to the High Court within fifteen days of the passing of the sentence.
answer.explanation: According to the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, an appeal against a sentence passed by an Anti-terrorism Court must be preferred within fifteen days of the sentence being passed.

citations.quote: An appeal under sub-section (1) may be preferred by a person sentenced by 1[an Anti- terrorismCourt] to 1[a High Court] within 2[fifteen] days of the passing of the sentence.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 ke tehat adalat witness ki shanakht (identity) ko mehfooz rakhne ke liye unki awaaz ya chehre ko badalne (morphing) ka hukm de sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Adalat witness ki hifazat aur unki shanakht chupane ke liye mukhtalif iqdamaat kar sakti hai, jin mein witness ki awaaz ko modulate karna aur unki tasveer ya awaaz ko morph karna shamil hai taake unki shanakht zahir na ho.

citations.quote: The kinds of measures that may be required to be taken in relation to a witness may include measures for securing one or more of the following: (v) that the witness’s voice is subjected to modulation to any specified
The Court in furtherance of the interest of justice may order the image and voice of the witness to be morphed so as to protect the identity of the same

If a wife exercises a delegated right to divorce or if parties seek to dissolve a marriage through means other than talaq, the procedural framework established in Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, applies with necessary modifications.
answer.explanation: The law mandates that for the dissolution of marriage other than by talaq, or when a wife exercises a delegated right of divorce, the provisions of Section 7 (which requires written notice to the Chairman and the other spouse) must be followed, mutatis mutandis.

citations.quote: Where the right to divorce has been duly delegated to the wife and she wishes to exercise that right, or where any of the parties to a marriage wishes to dissolve the marriage otherwise than by talaq, the provisions of section 7 shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as applicable, apply.

The same procedural framework, with necessary modifications, also applies to the dissolution of marriage otherwise than by talaq, including cases where the husband has delegated the right of divorce to the wife.

answer.short_answer: Agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Arbitration Council apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman muntakhib (elect) karegi.
answer.explanation: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 ke mutabiq, agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Council ke liye lazmi hai ke woh apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko is Ordinance ke maqasid ke liye Chairman chune.

citations.quote: Provided that where the Chairman of the Union Council is a non- Muslim, or he himself wishes to make an application to the Arbitration Council, or is, owing to illness or any other reason, unable to discharge the functions of Chairman, the Council shall elect one of its Muslim members as Chairman for the purposes of this Ordinance

answer.short_answer: جی ہاں، اینٹی منی لانڈرنگ ایکٹ 2010 کے تحت وفاقی حکومت کو ایکٹ کے نفاذ میں پیش آنے والی مشکلات کو دور کرنے کا اختیار حاصل ہے۔
answer.explanation: اگر ایکٹ کی دفعات پر عمل درآمد کے دوران کوئی مشکل پیدا ہو تو وفاقی حکومت سرکاری گزٹ میں حکم نامہ جاری کر کے ایسی دفعات وضع کر سکتی ہے جو ایکٹ کے منافی نہ ہوں اور مشکل کو دور کرنے کے لیے ضروری ہوں۔

citations.quote: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Federal Government may, by order, published in the official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act as may appear to be necessary for removing the difficulty.

answer.short_answer: If immediate action is required, an investigating officer may conduct a search and seizure with the prior permission of a senior officer of the concerned agency who is at least of BS-20 rank.
answer.explanation: While search and seizure powers generally require prior court permission, the Anti-Money Laundering Act provides a proviso for immediate action, allowing authorization from a senior officer of BS-20 rank or above. Additionally, the investigating officer must submit a report on the search and seizure to the head of the agency within forty-eight hours.

citations.quote: Provided that where immediate action is required, the powers of search and seizure shall be exercisable with prior permission of senior officer of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency not below the rank of an officer of BS-20.

The investigating officer shall, within forty-eight hours immediately after search and seizure, forward a copy of the report on search and seizure to the head of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency in a sealed envelope

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants ki assets ki tafseelat public ke liye available hoti hain.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants, unke spouse, aur dependent children ki assets ki declaration Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) ke paas digitally file ki jati hai aur yeh FBR ke zariye public ke liye available hoti hai.

citations.quote: the declaration of assets of a Civil Servant of BS-17 and above, his spouse and dependent children, including domestic and foreign assets and liabilities, as may be prescribed, shall be digitally filed with the Federal Board of Revenue and same shall be publicly available, through Federal Board of Revenue, in accordance with the rules as may be prescribed

answer.short_answer: Agar kisi civil servant ki post khatam ho jaye ya cadre mein posts kam ho jayein, toh aam taur par us shakhs ki naukri khatam ki jayegi jo us cadre ya service mein sab se junior ho.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, jab kisi post ke khatam hone ya cadre mein posts ki tadaad kam hone ki wajah se kisi civil servant ki naukri khatam karna zaroori ho, toh aam taur par sab se junior afsar ko farigh kiya jata hai.

citations.quote: Where, on the abolition of a post or reduction in the number of posts in a cadre or service, the services of a civil servant are required to be terminated, the person whose services are terminated shall ordinarily be the one who is the most junior in such cadre or service.

answer.short_answer: Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007, Section 19 ke tehat, Board tax-payers ke liye behtar sahuliyat faraham karne, ikhrajat ki direct cost reimbursement, aur public-private partnership ke tehat fiscal law se mutaliq khidmat faraham karne par munasib return on investment ya munafa hasil karne ke liye fees ya charges laga sakta hai.
answer.explanation: Section 19 Board ko ikhtiyar deta hai ke woh tax-payers ki behtari, kharchon ki wasooli, aur public-private partnership ke zariye di gayi khidmat par munasib munafa ya return hasil karne ke liye fees ya charges lagaye.

citations.quote: The Board may levy any fee or charges for making expenditure on the provision of enhanced facilities for the taxpayers, or direct cost reimbursement of expenses, and reasonable return on investment or profit; where services are provided in the matters relating to or under any fiscal law under public-private partnership.

answer.short_answer: The Appellate Authority is required to pass appropriate orders on an employee's appeal within ninety days of receiving the application.
answer.explanation: Under the National Command Authority Act, 2010, an employee aggrieved by an order or action regarding their terms and conditions of service may appeal to the prescribed Appellate Authority, which must decide the matter within ninety days.

citations.quote: The Appellate Authority may provide personal hearing to the applicant and pass appropriate orders within ninety days of the receipt of application.

answer.short_answer: The Provincial Government argued that the 2001 Ordinance redefined "licensee" to include entities using generators over 500 KW for self-use, thereby withdrawing previous protections and making them liable for electricity duty under Section 13.
answer.explanation: The Provincial Government contended that the 2001 Ordinance fundamentally changed the legal position, statutorily classifying those using generators over 500 KW for self-use as licensees and thus subject to the electricity duty.

citations.act_or_case: Govt. of Punjab v. M/s. Kunjah Textile Mills Ltd.
citations.quote: The case of the appellant Provincial Government, in a nutshell, is that up to 2001 the respondents may have been entitled to the benefit of the 1985 notification but thereafter the position changed fundamentally on account of the new definition of “licensee” substituted by the 2001 Ordinance. In terms of the last portion thereof (“any person generating the electric power from a generator having the capacity of more than five hundred kilowatt for self use”) they statutorily became licensees. Any protection that they may have had in terms of the 1985 notification stood withdrawn by the 2001 notification and thus they were liable to pay the electricity duty imposed by s. 13.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak aur Dr. Nasreen Kishwar ki promotion ke mamlay mein unhein nayi darkhwast (fresh application) jama karwane ki hidayat ki hai.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne Tribunal ka faisla kaladam qarar dete hue dono doctors ko Associate Professor (BPS-19) ke liye nayi darkhwast dene ka kaha hai, jis par Dean ko dossier foran IPC ko aglay ijlas mein ghor ke liye bhejna hoga.

citations.quote: Insofar as the claim of promotion of Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak [CPLA No.922-P/2024] and Dr. Nasreen Kishwar [CPLA No. 923-P/2025] is concerned, they agree to apply afresh for their promotion from BPS-18 to the post of Associate Professor (BPS-19)

On submission of fresh applications for promotion, the Dean of Khyber Girls Medical College Pakistan on receiving the applications, immediately forward the dossier for promotion to the IPC for consideration in the next meeting and communicate the decision to both the aforesaid doctors.

answer.short_answer: Trial Court ne 15 October 2005 ke waqiye mein mulzim ko umr qaid ki saza sunayi thi aur 300,000 rupay compensation ada karne ka hukum diya tha.
answer.explanation: Trial Court ne mulzim ko section 302(b) PPC ke tehat umr qaid ki saza di aur section 544-A Cr.PC ke tehat 300,000 rupay compensation ada karne ka hukum diya, jis ki adaigi na karne ki surat mein 6 mahine ki mazeed qaid (SI) bhugatni thi.

citations.act_or_case: Ghulam Sarwar Ghangro v. The State
citations.quote: The Trial Court vide judgment dated 20.09.2019 convicted petitioner under section 302(b) PPC and sentenced him to imprisonment for life and also directed to pay compensation of Rs.300,000/- to the legal heirs of deceased Abdul Waheed under section 544-A Cr.PC and in default thereof to further undergo SI for six months.

answer.short_answer: No, a party cannot introduce a new argument or set up a new case for the first time before the Supreme Court if it was not raised in the original pleadings or before the trial court.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court of Pakistan has established that parties are bound by their pleadings, and introducing a new case or argument that was not pleaded or supported by evidence at the trial stage is impermissible. Such attempts are considered afterthoughts and are rejected because they lack a foundation in the original dispute.

citations.act_or_case: Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others
citations.quote: It is, by now, settled that no party can be permitted to set up a new case for the first time before this Court, particularly one requiring factual inquiry. Equally settled is the principle that evidence beyond pleadings is of no legal consequence, and no finding can be founded on a case never pleaded.

citations.act_or_case: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others
citations.quote: A party cannot improve or alter its case beyond what has been originally set up, as the rule of secundum allegata et probata confines proof strictly to the facts alleged. ... Failure to plead essential or material facts is fatal, and a party is precluded from introducing new grounds or shifting its stance at a later stage of proceedings.

answer.short_answer: Police authorities are legally obligated to immediately execute an arrest once a court dismisses a pre-arrest bail application, without waiting for further instructions or assuming a stay exists.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court has clarified that the dismissal of pre-arrest bail means the accused is exposed to lawful arrest. Police must enforce these judicial orders promptly and in good faith, as the mere filing of a petition in a higher court does not act as an automatic stay or shield against arrest unless an express injunctive order is granted.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: This Court, therefore, finds it imperative to state clearly that investigating officers and police authorities are legally bound to act upon court orders dismissing pre-arrest bail immediately, without waiting for further instructions or presuming the existence of any stay where none has been granted.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: Absent such an order, a refusal of bail remains fully operative and must be implemented promptly and in good faith by investigating authorities.

answer.short_answer: Before ordering substituted service, the Court must be satisfied that the defendant is avoiding service or that the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way.
answer.explanation: The Court is required to satisfy itself that there is reason to believe the defendant is keeping out of the way to avoid service, or that ordinary service is not possible, and must adhere to the mandatory procedure prescribed by law.

citations.quote: Where the Court is satisfied that there is reason to believe that the defendant is keeping out of the way for the purpose of avoiding service, or that for any other reason the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way, the Court shall order for service of summons

the Court, before resorting to substituted service under Order V, Rule 20, C.P.C., must satisfy itself that ordinary service could not be effected and must adhere to the mandatory procedure prescribed by law.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court held that a cheque payment alone is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction in the absence of an agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence.
answer.explanation: The Court ruled that merely producing a cheque payment does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate the transfer of immovable property by an attorney to their sons, especially when there is no evidence of the principal's prior consent or approval for the transaction.

citations.act_or_case: Javed Iqbal & others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (deceased) through LRs
citations.quote: The alleged payment through cheque, made by the appellant (brother) in favour of the respondent (sister), is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction, particularly in the absence of any agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence reflecting a lawful bargain. Mere production of such payment, without establishing the underlying transaction, does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate an alienation of immovable property.

answer.short_answer: Under the 2001 Ordinance, a failure to collect advance tax triggers Section 161, which deems the person a taxpayer in default and subjects them to penal consequences.
answer.explanation: According to the Supreme Court, when a person required to collect advance tax fails to do so, Section 161 of the 2001 Ordinance applies, making them a deemed taxpayer in default. This further activates Section 163, which treats the required amount as tax due under an assessment order, leading to adverse penal consequences.

citations.quote: This alleged failure, according to the Department, triggered s. 161 of the 2001 Ordinance which, inter alia, applies when a person who is required to deduct or collect advance tax fails to do so. Such failure makes that person a deemed taxpayer in default and, inter alia, activates s. 163 which provides as follows: “The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount required to be paid to the Commissioner under this Division as if it were tax due under an assessment order”.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ruled that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) was justified and set aside the lower courts' judgments that had directed a refund.
answer.explanation: The Court held that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee was reasonable under the circumstances and dismissed the respondent company's claim for damages, thereby overturning the previous orders requiring the refund of the guarantee.

citations.act_or_case: Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. M/s
citations.quote: The forfeiture of the entire amount of the performance guarantee by TCP was justified and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case.

citations.act_or_case: Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. M/s
citations.quote: The judgments of the learned Single Judge and the Division Bench of the Sindh High Court, insofar as they direct refund of the performance guarantee, are hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne yeh observation di hai ke agar petitioner apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit wapas nahi leta, toh Court apne faislay par nazar-e-sani (review) karegi.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke petitioner ne apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit is bunyad par file kiya tha ke woh kama rahi hai. Court ne wazeh kiya ke agar petitioner ne yeh suit wapas na liya, toh yeh aml Court ko apne faislay par nazar-e-sani karne par majboor karega.

citations.act_or_case: Sadiq Subhani v. Sadia Arooj and others

answer.short_answer: Infertility, or the suspicion thereof, does not constitute a valid legal ground to deny a woman her dower or maintenance.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court of Pakistan has clarified that infertility cannot be used as a weapon against women in litigation, and it is not a permissible basis for withholding dower or maintenance, as doing so is considered an abuse of the legal process and an affront to human dignity.

citations.act_or_case: Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others
citations.quote: However, it must be acknowledged without equivocation that infertility, even if present, is no ground to deny a woman her dower or maintenance.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne High Court ke suit decree karne ke faislay ko ikhtiyar se bahar qarar dete hue set-aside kar diya aur mamla dobara Family Court ko bhej diya.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne wazeh kiya ke High Court apni constitutional jurisdiction ka istemal karte hue Family Court ke ikhtiyarat khud nahi sambhal sakti aur na hi suit decree kar sakti hai. Is liye, High Court ka suit decree karne ka faisla set-aside kar diya gaya aur case ko Family Court mein naye sire se faislay ke liye remand kar diya gaya.

citations.quote: However, as regards the decision of the High Court to decree respondent No.1’s suit, the same being beyond the jurisdiction of the High Court, is liable to be set-aside. Consequently, leave to appeal is granted only to the extent of the High Court’s decision to decree the suit; the petition is converted into an appeal to the said extent only and allowed; and the matter is remanded to the Family Court for a decision afresh
The High Court in exercise of its Constitutional jurisdiction cannot arrogate to itself the powers of a family Court and issue decrees.

answer.short_answer: The primary legal controversy concerns the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Articles 51(6)(d), 51(6)(e), and 106(3)(c) of the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court identified that the core issue involves determining how these reserved seats are to be allocated to political parties based on their numerical strength in the respective houses, as mandated by the Constitution.

citations.quote: The core controversy requiring resolution relates to the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Article 51(6)(d) and (e) and Article 106(3)(c) of the Constitution, respectively.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court of Pakistan converted the civil petitions into appeals, allowed them, set aside the impugned judgment of the Service Tribunal, and restored the seniority of the petitioners to its original condition.
answer.explanation: The Court found that the petitioners had successfully made a case for interference, leading to the reversal of the Tribunal's decision which had previously set aside the seniority list.

citations.quote: As a consequence thereof, we convert these civil petitions into appeals and allow them. Consequently, the impugned judgment of the learned Tribunal is set aside and the seniority of the petitioners is restored to its original condition.

answer.short_answer: The accused, Allah Yar, filed an application for a medical board before the Area Magistrate, which was dismissed on May 21, 2026; he then successfully challenged this in a revision petition before the Additional Sessions Judge, whose order was subsequently set aside by the High Court.
answer.explanation: The accused initially applied to the Area Magistrate for a medical board to examine Medico-Legal Certificates, but the Magistrate dismissed the application on May 21, 2026. The accused then filed a revision petition, which the Additional Sessions Judge allowed on June 15, 2026. However, the High Court later set aside the Additional Sessions Judge's order, ruling that the Magistrate acted as a persona designata and that the order was not subject to revisional jurisdiction.

citations.quote: Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed application before learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala for constituting medical board regarding Medico-Legal Examination Certificates... which was dismissed vide order dated: 21.05.2026... Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed revision petition against aforesaid order dated: 21.05.2026... which was allowed vide order dated: 15.06.2026

Admittedly, while conducting proceedings on an application seeking medical re-examination of an injured, the Magistrate does not act as a Criminal Court but in the capacity of a persona designata. Consequently, the order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala was administrative/ executive in nature and, therefore, was not amenable to revisional jurisdiction... Resultantly, the instant criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed and impugned order dated 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala is hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Lahore High Court ne acquired land ka compensation Rs. 5,00,000/- per marla ke uniform rate par tay kiya.
answer.explanation: Court ne yeh faisla land ki location, potential, prevailing market conditions, aur judicial precedents ko madd-e-nazar rakhte hue kiya, kyunke nichli adalat ne land ki sahi market value ka andaza nahi lagaya tha.

citations.quote: Keeping in view the totality of circumstances, the location and potential of the acquired land, the prevailing market conditions at the relevant time and the judicial precedents referred to hereinabove, we are of the considered opinion that the ends of justice would be adequately met by assessing the entire land at a uniform rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per marla.

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court suggested allowing the petitioner to withdraw the suit with permission to file a fresh one on the same cause of action by impleading the necessary parties.
answer.explanation: The Court determined that because the suit was filed without necessary parties, allowing them to be impleaded at that stage would necessitate amending pleadings, framing fresh issues, and re-recording evidence, which would be inefficient. Consequently, the Court proposed that the petitioner withdraw the suit and file a new one, a course of action to which both parties agreed.

citations.act_or_case: Muhammad Usman v. NADRA through its Chairman, NSRC, Islamabad and 2 others
citations.quote: In view thereof, the alternate procedure available before this Court for reaching just conclusion of the matter would be to allow the petitioner to withdraw the suit and file afresh one on the basis of same cause of action by impleading necessary parties referred to in the judgments passed by the courts below. When confronted, both the sides have no objection to the said course of action.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a person who provides necessaries to someone incapable of contracting is entitled to be reimbursed from that individual's property.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a person who is incapable of entering into a contract, or anyone they are legally bound to support, is supplied with necessaries suited to their condition in life, the supplier has a legal right to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person.

citations.quote: If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.

answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke SRPO ke tehat concurrent findings ko set aside karne ke mamlay mein High Court ko dobara ghaur karne ki zaroorat hai, is liye Supreme Court ne High Court ke impugned judgment ko set aside kar diya aur mamlay ko 6 mahine ke andar naye siray se faisla karne ki hidayat ki.
